title: Every Diamond PAU controller function is gated by the same three checks in the same order
content:
Across every operational flow in this section the Atlas repeats one three-part template. Taking the Aave deposit as representative: A.2.2.10.1.1.1.2.5.2.2.1.1 restricts initiation to an address holding `ALLOCATOR_ROLE` calling the Controller; A.2.2.10.1.1.1.2.5.2.2.1.2 subjects the call to a rate limit "enforced automatically within the call; the transaction reverts if the amount exceeds the current rate limit"; A.2.2.10.1.1.1.2.5.2.2.1.3 requires that "the aTokens received must satisfy the configured maximum slippage."

The identical shape recurs for USDS mint and burn (…2.1.1.1–3, …2.1.2.1–3) and for Basin deposit and withdraw (…2.3.1.1–3, …2.3.2.1–3). The Controller's only job is dispatch: A.2.2.10.1.1.1.2.5.2 states it "dispatches each function to the corresponding Facet contract, which performs the operation on behalf of the ALM Proxy."

The checks are chosen to be independent failure domains — *who* may act, *how much* may move, and *at what price* — so no single compromised element authorizes a harmful transaction. A stolen relayer key still faces the rate limit; a mispriced or manipulated venue still faces the slippage bound.

Because enforcement lives in the contracts rather than in relayer software, the pattern also fixes what reviewers must verify for each new Facet: the role gate and limit check are structural, leaving only the execution-quality guard as integration-specific work.
description: Role gate, then an automatic rate-limit revert, then an execution-quality bound checked inside the Facet — repeated identically across the USDS, Aave and Basin flows.
